title: Layer 2 engine: snapshot discovery per owning session for the Layer 1 View route
description:
Spec S19; the signed-off mockup is plans/layer2-mockup/ (index.html + fixture.js + app.js, 43 headless checks in jfred/scripts/visual/mockup.ts via `npm run visual:mockup`). Layer 2 is the SNAPSHOT layer — the JSONL layer was dropped, not deferred (second renumbering pass in the spec's Key Decisions).

The engine core already exists and must be REUSED, not rewritten: jfred/src/layered_snapshot_beacons.ts's collectSnapshotBeaconNodes (task 201, spec S4) already walks buildBackupTimeline(records, findCwd(records)) and resolves every non-null backupFileName through a per-OWNING-SESSION BackupReader — which is the whole point, because `abc123@v2` recurs across sessions with DIFFERENT bytes. What does NOT exist is a path from that to the Layer 1 View route: jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts reads NO JSONL at all by design (S18), so Layer 2 is the item that introduces JSONL and file-history as inputs to that route.

THE WORK: new jfred/src/layer1_snapshots.ts exporting a function that takes the JSONL session file paths and the file-history root(s) and returns, per ABSOLUTE file path, a list of SnapshotPlacement { path, version, instant, sessionId, sessionFile, line, backupFileName } ordered by instant. Reuse what is there: parse each transcript with jfred/src/parse/loadTranscript.ts, build the reader with buildSidecarReader(records, sources) or createSidecarReader(sessionId, root) from jfred/src/reconstruction_sidecar_reader.ts, and take the points from buildBackupTimeline (BackupPoint = { backupTime, backupFileName | null, sessionId }). `version` is the `@vN` suffix parsed off backupFileName and is numbered PER SESSION — never treat it as a global identity; the mockup fixture deliberately carries src/util.ts @v2 from b21d84c5 AND a different @v2 from d4a06b8f for exactly this reason. Version 1 carries a null backupFileName (no blob) and is SKIPPED, the same rule collectSnapshotBeaconNodes already applies. `line` is the transcript line the backup point was recorded at — task 311 needs it to pick the customTitle in effect.

Do NOT read blob bytes here. The wire carries PLACEMENTS only and the bytes are fetched on demand by task 313: a project with hundreds of snapshots would otherwise pay a full read on every view build, which already runs ~10 s.

Root discovery: resolveFileHistoryRoot(records), deriveSiblingFileHistoryRoot(projectsDir) and deriveFileHistoryRootFromRecords already exist in jfred/src/reconstruction_sidecar_reader.ts — an explicitly-supplied root WINS and discovery is the fallback (the S1 rule).

VERIFY: unit test with two fixture sessions using the same `@vN` name for different bytes — each placement carries its own sessionId, and reading through each session's reader yields that session's bytes. Second test: a null-backupFileName v1 produces no placement. TRAP: the file-history reader falls back to the LIVE ~/.claude/file-history when a test does not load through loadTranscript, so a careless test silently reads the developer's real machine and passes for the wrong reason.

title: Layer 2 engine: JSONL session metadata and the customTitle in effect at a line
description:
Spec S19, "JSONL Nav row order" and "Snapshot node click". Two consumers need this. The JSONL Nav row is three parts — truncated `<filename>.jsonl`, then the session's customTitle values deduped (omitted when it has none), then `<start timestamp> · N files`. The snapshot drawer header reads `<filename> Snapshot - <customTitle>`, where that title is the one IN EFFECT OVER THE LINE RANGE WHERE THE SNAPSHOT OCCURRED, not the session's first or last. A user may rename a session more than once, so a session's title is a FUNCTION OF POSITION in the file; picking the wrong one attributes a snapshot to work it has nothing to do with. The mockup fixture carries session b21d84c5 with two titles over two line ranges and a snapshot inside each, precisely so a grab-the-first or grab-the-last implementation is visibly wrong.

THE WORK: new jfred/src/layer1_sessions.ts exporting (a) a builder returning, per session file, { file, sessionId, started, ended, paths[], titles: [{ fromLine, title }] } and (b) a pure `titleInEffectAtLine(titles, line)` returning the last title whose fromLine <= line, or undefined when the session was not yet named at that point. The record already parses: RecordType.customTitle = "custom-title" in jfred/src/structures/vocabulary.ts, the title rides on the record's `n` key, and jfred/src/reconstruction_json.ts already walks them. `started` and `ended` are the session's FIRST and LAST record instants — deliberately NOT the instants of the files it touched, because the Nav band has to be able to open before the first write and close after the last one (the mockup fixture states this rule explicitly). `paths` is what the session wrote, which is all task 292's filter needs; the timeline those paths draw still comes from the repo and the disk, so a file keeps its whole history even when the session touched it once.

VERIFY: unit tests — a session with two titles returns the FIRST for a line inside range one and the SECOND for a line inside range two; a line before the first custom-title record returns undefined; an unnamed session yields an empty titles list. Deduping is a DISPLAY concern that belongs to the Nav row, so the builder returns every range rather than a deduped set — the drawer needs the ranges the Nav throws away.

title: Layer 2 engine: snapshot nodes on the Layer 1 wire, ruler and shared axis
description:
Spec S19. Extend jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts's Layer1WireView so every pair — and every DISK ORPHAN, since a file can be snapshotted without being in the repo — carries `snapshots: Layer1WireSnapshot[]`, where Layer1WireSnapshot extends Layer1WireInstant with { version, sessionFile, sessionId, line }. The route gains `?jsonl=` and `?snapshots=` params for the session and file-history roots (task 310's inputs) and round-trips them through the URL exactly as ?dir=&repo=&ref=&time= already do, so a Layer 2 view stays one shareable link; tasks 295 and 296's pickers write into these same params.

The payload ALWAYS carries snapshots regardless of the selected layer. The layer switcher is a client-side show/hide (task 314), and refetching on toggle would pay the ~10 s build twice.

Snapshot instants are REAL ruler entries: they join the capped-gap ladder, they get ticks, and they count toward Layer1WireRulerTick.eventCount. So they must flow through layOutNodeLadders in jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-axis.ts — the module the server and the client SHARE — not be bolted on afterwards. Per the S19 CORRECTION of 2026-07-27, a pre-commit snapshot does NOT pull a bubble's anchor earlier: `born <= snapshot <= mtime` is physics and `born` is itself a node, so no snapshot can ever be a bubble's earliest node; what it does instead is take a ruler entry above every commit, which lengthens the ladder below it. Add a progress label for the new stage beside the existing LAYER1_PROGRESS_LABEL_* constants — the snapshot read is new cost in a build that already runs ~10 s, and this project's standing rule is that anything slow shows progress.

TRAPS. (1) jfred/webapp/layer1-wire.ts and jfred/webapp/layer1-filter.ts MIRROR the server's ladder so a folder filter can re-layout client-side; if the mirror does not add snapshots identically, a filtered view's offsets silently disagree with the shipped ones. (2) Task 259's tie-group markers read instants off the ladder, so extra nodes change which nodes group. (3) countRowsPerInstant in layer1-ruler-axis.ts measures per-instant row demand from the ladders, so adding nodes changes ruler spacing and every offset after it — the existing placement tests' hand-derived ladders will have to be redone. (4) viewer_api_layer1.ts is near the 250-line cap, so the new behaviour goes in a NEW module.

VERIFY: unit tests — an instant occupied ONLY by a snapshot appears in `ruler`; eventCount at a shared instant counts the snapshot alongside the commit or disk node (the mockup's src/index.ts @v3 lands exactly ON its mtime, inside a task-259 tie); a snapshot-free pair's wire shape is unchanged from today; the same fixture through the client mirror produces the same offsets as the server.

title: Layer 2 engine: serve snapshot bytes from /api/layer1-file by owning session
description:
Spec S19. jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_file.ts today has two forms, one per node kind Layer 1 draws — a commit node reads its blob out of git (`?repo=&path=&hash=`), the on-disk node reads the working-tree bytes (`?dir=&path=`). Layer 2 adds a third node kind, so it adds a third form: the snapshot node reads its blob out of the OWNING SESSION's file-history sidecar, resolved through createSidecarReader(sessionId, root) from jfred/src/reconstruction_sidecar_reader.ts — the same reader task 310 uses.

The params must carry the SESSION IDENTITY, never just the blob name. `abc123@v2` recurs across sessions with different bytes, so a lookup by name alone serves the wrong file's contents with no visible error — the failure is silent and looks like a reconstruction bug rather than a routing one.

Both existing forms treat their inputs as TRUST BOUNDARIES and the new one must too: COMMIT_HASH_PATTERN guards the hash, and an explicit prefix-with-separator check guards the working-tree path (the separator is load-bearing — without it "/tmp/ab" passes a startsWith against "/tmp/a"). The blob name and the session id both reach the filesystem from a URL, so validate their shape before any read and refuse a name that escapes the file-history root. spawnSync stays in ARGUMENT-ARRAY form (the task-235 rule); nothing here may be parsed by a shell.

VERIFY: route test — the same `@vN` name under two different session ids returns two different bodies; a name containing `..` is refused; an unknown session id is a clean 4xx, not a stack trace.

title: Layer 2 page: make the [2] layer button live and drop [3]
description:
Spec S19, "Same page, one switcher". Layer 2 is NOT a second page. jfred/webapp/layer1.html lines 32-35 still carry the PRE-RENUMBERING labels — `[2] title="Layer 2 adds JSONL-derived start points"` and `[3] title="Layer 3 adds file-history snapshots"` — both wrong since the JSONL layer was dropped rather than deferred. The `[3]` button goes away entirely (unassigned), `[2]` loses its `.uncomputed` class, and its tooltip becomes "Layer 2 adds file-history snapshots", matching the signed-off mockup at plans/layer2-mockup/index.html.

Toggling is CLIENT-SIDE ONLY — no refetch, because task 312 always ships the snapshots. Layer 1 hides snapshot nodes AND the ruler entries only a snapshot occupies; Layer 2 shows them on the SAME bubbles against the SAME ruler. Nothing else may change between the two states: a file with no snapshots renders at Layer 2 exactly as it does at Layer 1 — no node, and no "no snapshots available" text, which S18 retired per the #221 supersession.

TRAP: jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts is AT the 250-line cap, so the switcher's wiring goes in a NEW module (precedent: layer1-time-toggle.ts, layer1-zoom.ts), and layer1-page.ts boots at MODULE SCOPE, so importing it twice double-wires every listener.

VERIFY: toggle 1 → 2 → 1 and diff the rendered DOM — only snapshot nodes and snapshot-only ruler rows appear and disappear; bubble anchors, spans and every other offset are unchanged.

title: Layer 2 page: draw 📸 snapshot nodes on the file bubbles
description:
Spec S19, "Snapshot nodes". One node per snapshot version — @v1, @v2, … — placed at its own axisPx on its file's bubble, marked with a CAMERA EMOJI (📸, user-chosen 2026-07-27) so it is distinguishable at a glance from a commit node and from the on-disk node, and carrying its OWNING SESSION on the node's detail. Follow the signed-off mockup's placement, class names and ids (plans/layer2-mockup/app.js and index.html) rather than re-designing them — the mockup is the reference the user signed off on, exactly as layer1-mockup.html was for S18.

The bubble builder is buildPairWidget in jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts, the styles live in jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css, and the always-visible legend in layer1.html gains a snapshot swatch (spec S12 — the legend is not optional).

The node must carry enough identity in the DOM for tasks 316 and 317 to act on it without a second fetch: the version, the owning session file, and the transcript line, since the drawer header's title lookup keys on the line. Follow the task-280 precedent and put these in `data-` attributes, NOT `title` — the user rejected native tooltips (delayed, unstyled, gone on the first mouse move), which is why the full path already moved to `data-path`.

TRAPS: layer1-page.ts is AT the 250-line cap, so this goes in a new module; task 259's tie groups read instants off the ladder, so a snapshot sharing an instant with a commit or the mtime — the mockup's src/index.ts @v3 does exactly this — must land in the tie group's row slots rather than on top of its neighbour.

VERIFY: headless check against the real page — a snapshotted file shows one 📸 node per snapshot at the offsets the wire shipped; a snapshot-free file's bubble is unchanged from Layer 1; a snapshot sharing an instant with another node sits one row apart from it, not overlapping.

title: Layer 2 page: expanded ruler tick lists snapshot rows, clicking one highlights its JSONL
description:
Spec S19, "Ruler expand rows" and "Ruler snapshot row → JSONL Nav highlight". Task 284's expanded tick already lists one row per event as `<filename> <type identifier slug>`, where a commit's slug is the first 8 characters of its hash. A snapshot's slug is `@vN 📸` — the SAME row shape, so the list stays one column of filenames with a trailing identifier and needs NO new layout. The code is jfred/webapp/layer1-tick-files.ts: TickEvent, describeDrawnElement, buildTickFileButton, buildTickFileList and listEventsAtRow. Note a printed ruler row can stand for SEVERAL instants (task 268's merge), which is why RulerRow already carries every offset it absorbed.

Clicking a snapshot row HIGHLIGHTS, BUT DOES NOT SELECT, the JSONL that snapshot came from in the JSONL Nav — a DIFFERENT COLOUR from the selection colour, since selecting is what filters the view and this must not. The highlight FADES OUT after a few seconds: its whole job is to answer "where did this come from", and a persistent mark would keep pulling the eye off the timeline.

Build the flash as ONE exported mechanism here; task 317 is its second caller ("one mechanism, two callers" — S19). The mockup's implementation is the reference, including its `flash` and `flash-lead` classes, which exist partly so a headless check can observe which row led.

VERIFY: headless check — an expanded tick containing a snapshot shows a `<filename> @vN 📸` row; clicking it adds the highlight class to the right session row in the JSONL Nav, does NOT change the selection or the filter, and the class is gone after the fade. TRAP found while building the mockup: the flash must CLEAR the previous lead marker on every invocation, or two rapid clicks leave two leads marked.

title: Layer 2 page: snapshot node click opens the drawer with the title in effect and flashes its JSONL
description:
Spec S19, "Snapshot node click". Clicking a snapshot node does TWO things.

(1) It opens task 257's Detail drawer — jfred/webapp/layer1-drawer.ts, whose describeNode builds the /api/layer1-file params and the header — on that snapshot's bytes, via task 313's third form, with the header reading `<filename> Snapshot - <customTitle>`. That customTitle is the one IN EFFECT OVER THE JSONL LINE RANGE WHERE THE SNAPSHOT OCCURRED (task 311's titleInEffectAtLine), NOT the session's first or last: a user may rename a session more than once, so a session's title is a function of position in the file, and picking the wrong one attributes a snapshot to work it has nothing to do with.

(2) It FLASHES the owning session in the JSONL Nav — the identical highlight-then-fade task 316 builds, CALLED here, not re-implemented.

The drawer is a third flex child of .stagewrap rather than an overlay, so opening it SHRINKS the timeline pane instead of covering the render it describes, and the clicked node is re-centred against the POST-reflow layout — which is why .drawer carries no width transition. Its numbered-line renderer was deliberately COPIED out of the classic Revision View rather than imported (user-directed 2026-07-27): importing drags app-routes → inspector → timeline-* into a page that loads only layer1-*.js. Do not "fix" that by importing.

VERIFY: headless check against the real page — clicking a snapshot node from a session that was renamed part-way through yields the title in effect at THAT snapshot's line, and clicking the other snapshot in the same session yields the OTHER title; the drawer body is the OWNING session's bytes for a `@vN` name that collides across sessions; the owning session flashes in the Nav.

title: Layer 2 verification: port the mockup's headless checks onto the real page with real data
description:
Project rule (CLAUDE.md, "Verification Before Reporting Done"): UI work is not done until it is verified in a real browser via a headless CDP smoke test with REAL data — if a fix is visual, DOM assertions alone do not settle it. The mockup already carries 43 checks in jfred/scripts/visual/mockup.ts with mockup-checks.ts and mockup-checks-nav.ts, run by `npm run visual:mockup`, but those assert against plans/layer2-mockup/ fixtures. This task ports the Layer 2 ones onto the REAL page (jfred/webapp/layer1.html served by the viewer), driven against a real project folder, repo, JSONL source and file-history root, alongside the existing `npm run visual` Layer 1 loop.

Cover, at minimum, S19's verify list: the [2] button is live and [3] is gone; toggling 1 ↔ 2 adds and removes snapshot nodes and the ruler entries only a snapshot occupies, and NOTHING else changes; a snapshot node carries 📸; clicking it opens the drawer headed `<filename> Snapshot - <the customTitle in effect at that point in the session>` while flashing its JSONL in the Nav; an expanded ruler tick lists snapshot rows as `<filename> @vN 📸`; clicking one highlights its JSONL in a non-selection colour that fades; JSONL Nav rows read filename / customTitles / timestamp · files; the two same-`@vN`-different-bytes snapshots are distinguishable; a snapshot-free file is unchanged from Layer 1.

TRAPS from the Layer 1 visual loop: the Chrome profile removal races SIGKILL; a filtered view has no `.tick.multi`; and a STALE viewer left running on the dev port reads as the feature being broken, so the check must cold-start its own server rather than assume one.

title: Fixture mode: serve the REAL Layer 1 page from canned payloads, so the mockup stops needing to be kept in sync
description:
User-directed 2026-07-29, from the user's own inquiry: "Can we stop using the mockup and instead use the real web app but feed the real web app with the fixture data, so we stop having to keep the mockup in sync with the real webapp?" The concrete cost being paid today is that `plans/layer2-mockup/` re-implements the File Nav, ruler, bubbles, drawer and diff pair in plain JS beside the real `webapp/` versions, so every approved mockup behaviour then has to be ported by hand — and the two do not line up: "the positioning of several items is not identical and reporting the differences is not worth the time or tokens".

DECISION (user, 2026-07-29): SERVER-SIDE stub routes, NOT a client-side static-data shim. `webapp/` is NOT touched by this task. That is the whole point of the choice — the page under review must be byte-identical to the production page, so the mockup and the app cannot differ in CSS, in component structure, or in the axis arithmetic. A client-side shim was considered and rejected here: it would add a branch to shipping client code and would still not fix positioning, because position comes from `webapp/layer1-ruler-axis.ts` and `webapp/layer1-styles.css`. (It would have had one extra payoff — a static GitHub Pages demo of the real page, which is what the now-closed task #17 originally wanted and what #222 wants to host. If that demo is ever wanted, it is a SEPARATE task built on top of this one, not a reason to change this one.)

THE SEAM, ALREADY BUILT. `dispatchLayer1Route` in jfred/src/viewer_server_layer1_routes.ts is a single function that owns every Layer 1 route and returns whether it OWNED the request, so the caller's chain falls through unchanged when it did not. Fixture mode is therefore ONE branch at the top of that function, routing to a fixture handler instead of the real ones. Note its header comment says "six HTTP routes" and it now dispatches EIGHT — POST `/api/layer1-settings`, GET `/api/layer1-settings`, `/api/layer1-view`, `/api/layer1-refs`, `/api/layer1-sessions`, `/api/layer1-file`, `/api/layer1-diff`, `/api/scan-source` — so fix that comment while you are in there. `/api/pick-folder` is registered in jfred/src/viewer_server.ts and does NOT go through the dispatcher; an OS folder dialog is meaningless against a fixture, so decide and document whether it stays live (harmless) or refuses in fixture mode.

THE WORK. (1) New jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_fixture.ts holding the canned payloads for those eight routes. (2) One branch in `dispatchLayer1Route`. (3) A switch that is OFF by default and cannot be hit accidentally while looking at a real project — a `--fixture` argument to the viewer is the obvious shape; if a query param is used instead it must not be reachable from any link the normal page builds.

THE DATA. Translate `plans/layer2-mockup/fixture.js` — its `COMMITS`, `DISK`, `SESSIONS` and `SNAPSHOTS` arrays — into the wire shapes in jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts: `Layer1WireView` = { pairs, gitOrphans, diskOrphans, ruler }. Do NOT hand-compute the offsets: `Layer1WireInstant` carries `axisPx`, the S18 ruler ACCUMULATES, and `layOutNodeLadders` in jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-axis.ts is the one function the server and client already share to produce them — the fixture must go THROUGH it, or the page will disagree with itself the moment a folder filter re-lays out client-side. Carry the fixture's own invariants across, because they are what make the review meaningful: `born <= snapshot <= mtime`; one file carrying the same `@vN` from two different sessions with DIFFERENT bytes; one session carrying two `customTitle` values over two line ranges with a snapshot inside each; and a file with NO snapshots, which must render exactly as it does at Layer 1. The fixture also self-checks on load today — keep an equivalent assertion, since a fixture that violates its own rules is worse than no fixture.

THE HARNESS. Re-point jfred/scripts/visual/mockup.ts at the real page in fixture mode instead of serving `plans/layer2-mockup/` over `python3 -m http.server`. The 92 checks now in jfred/scripts/visual/mockup-checks.ts, mockup-checks-nav.ts and mockup-checks-diff.ts ARE the acceptance list for this task: a check that passed against the mockup and fails against the real page is either a real gap in the page or a mockup behaviour that was never ported, and each one must be classified as such rather than deleted. `scripts/visual/run.ts` (the existing six-state real-viewer loop) is the precedent for booting the server from a check script.

SCOPE LIMIT, DELIBERATE. Layer 2 does not exist in the real page yet — that is tasks #310-#318, none started. So fixture mode ships covering LAYER 1 ONLY, and `plans/layer2-mockup/` stays alive for Layer 2 review until roughly #315. It must not be deleted by this task. What this task buys immediately is that every FUTURE Layer 1 change is reviewed on the real page, and that #310-#318 are built against a page the user can actually see.

WHY IT BLOCKS #310 (user-directed 2026-07-29): the alternative was finishing all nine Layer 2 tasks in the mockup first, which would pay the porting tax nine more times — exactly the tax this task exists to stop.

VERIFY: `npm run viewer` with the flag serves /layer1.html rendering the fixture with no project folder, no git repo and no JSONL on disk; `webapp/` has zero changes in the diff; the flag off is byte-identical behaviour to today (a real project view is unaffected); the re-pointed check script runs green, with any check that could not be carried over listed and classified in the task's closure note rather than silently dropped.
